pr-1NMP.title: Landscape: noticeably drier in the south
pr-1NMP.summary: The south of the island often looks clearly drier than the rest.

pr-2LXU.title: Landscape: flat plains or rolling hills on coasts
pr-2LXU.summary: Both the north and south coasts are mostly flat coastal plains or gentle rolling hills.

pr-4QdF.title: Coverage: US territory
pr-4QdF.summary: An overseas territory of the United States, so it counts as the US for country streaks.

pr-8rin.title: Sign: unique highway shields
pr-8rin.summary: Highway route shields in four styles: primary, primary urban, secondary and tertiary. These shapes do not appear in any other US state or territory.

differs.how: No US state uses these shield designs

pr-CcDj.title: Landscape: mountains in the middle, highways only
pr-CcDj.summary: The mountains are in the middle of the island, and coverage there is mostly limited to divided highways.

pr-FSsp.title: Shops: American store chains
pr-FSsp.summary: US chains such as Wal-Mart are very common. This separates it from nearby Latin American countries, where US stores are rare.

pr-MALI.title: Sign: stop sign says PARE
pr-MALI.summary: Stop signs read PARE instead of STOP. The same word is used all over South America and in the Dominican Republic.

pr-Npkn.title: Google car: older camera, antenna front right
pr-Npkn.summary: The older Gen 3 car (blurrier, softer colours) with an antenna at the front right, tipped with a small white dot. Guam and the Northern Marianas cars have a similar antenna, so check other clues.

differs.how: Guam car also has a front-right antenna, so use other clues

pr-TIjg.title: Google car: wide blur, antenna, low camera
pr-TIjg.summary: Almost all coverage uses a small low camera: a wide, rounded blur at the bottom and often a visible antenna. It is lower and rounder than the blur of a pickup truck car.

pr-avsT.title: Sign: Spanish where US signs use English
pr-avsT.summary: Signs are commonly in Spanish rather than English, which sets it apart from mainland US roads.

pr-eA8V.title: Coverage: rural roads are big divided highways
pr-eA8V.summary: In the countryside much of the coverage is on large divided highways.

pr-hatM.title: Architecture: narrow streets, colourful old town
pr-hatM.summary: In the north-west tip of the capital: very narrow streets, colourful buildings, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque styles, and some brick streets.

pr-m45n.title: Houses: concrete, flat roofs, metal gates
pr-m45n.summary: Most homes are concrete with flat roofs, and metal gates in front are common, especially in towns. Homes elsewhere in Latin America can look similar.

pr-nXMf.title: Sign: US speed limit sign in Spanish
pr-nXMf.summary: Speed limit signs have the same shape and size as in the mainland US, but the text is always in Spanish.

differs.how: US speed signs use English text

pr-nsPb.title: Architecture: Victorian-Spanish wood and masonry
pr-nsPb.summary: In the southern city of Ponce, buildings mix Victorian and Spanish Revival styles, typically wood and masonry.

pr-sbGW.title: Kilometre marker: tall, green, vertical number
pr-sbGW.summary: A tall green marker with km at the top and a large number written vertically below it.

pr-x00D.title: Plate: rarely a front plate
pr-x00D.summary: Front plates are not required, so cars without one are the norm. This helps tell it apart from Guam and the Northern Marianas.

differs.how: Guam cars usually have front plates
Northern Marianas cars usually have front plates

pr-zV2D.title: Phone numbers: area code (787)
pr-zV2D.summary: Phone numbers written (787) XXX-XXXX cover the whole island. The code 939 also appears but is much rarer.
